questions.question: A garden 12 m by 8 m has a path 1 m wide around it. Find the area of the path and explain a common error.
questions.expected_answer: The outer rectangle is 14 m by 10 m, area 140 square metres, and the garden is 96 square metres, so the path is 44 square metres. A common error is adding the path width only once to each dimension, or multiplying the garden's perimeter by the width and forgetting the four corner squares.

questions.question: A track has straights of 80 m and semicircular ends of radius 30 m. Find the length of its inside edge.
questions.expected_answer: The two straights give 160 m and the two semicircles together make a full circle of circumference 60 pi, about 188,50 m, so the inside edge is about 348,50 m.

questions.question: Why are numbers of tiles or tins always rounded up?
questions.expected_answer: Because they are bought as whole items, and rounding down would leave the job short. Even 15,4 boxes means 16 boxes must be bought.
